A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DPsurv and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Retained content can be matched despite substantial restructuring, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-fold survival-prediction experiments on five TCGA cohorts, including C-index, IBS, IBLL, calibration plots, and pathological interpretation examples.

after.justification: v2 reports revised survival-prediction results and additional original ablations, sensitivity tests, feature-extractor comparisons, runtime measurements, and pathologist coherence ratings.

M1.justification: Equation 15 removes the precision and distance-decay regularization terms, ξR1 and ρR2, leaving the weighted survival likelihood objective. The patch-prototype GMM, component-prototype evidence fusion, mixture aggregation, and prediction procedures remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 Appendix B.1 and v2 Appendix G.1 report the same BRCA, BLCA, LUAD, UCEC, and KIRC cohorts with identical patient and WSI counts. The added analyses reuse this coverage; CONCH changes the feature extractor, while additional pathologist-rated examples extend the existing interpretability evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated MC Dropout and Deep Ensemble comparators in Appendix K, Table 9 and Figure 7. The nine principal baselines are retained. DSMIL is not newly evaluated: it already appears in v1's result tables and Appendix B.2 despite its omission from the main baseline-list paragraph.

E3.justification: v2 replaces cohort-specific learning rates with 1e-4, changes DPsurv's training budget from 50 to 30 epochs and λ from 0.1 to 0.5, and selects K from {1,2,3,4} through validation/early stopping instead of the earlier cohort/fold-size choices. It newly specifies a 15% validation holdout and explicitly reports retraining baselines under the shared selection protocol. New protocols include fixed-configuration ablations, CONCH evaluation on UCEC, and a two-pathologist, 10-point coherence assessment.

E4.justification: v1 has qualitative interpretation examples but no component-ablation or hyperparameter-sensitivity experiments. v2 adds component ablations in Table 2, K/C/λ/α sensitivity tests in Tables 6–7, feature-extractor robustness in Table 3, additional interpretation examples and expert ratings in Appendix I, and a targeted analysis of the lowest-rated case in Appendix L.

E5.justification: Five-fold cross-validation and mean-with-±-dispersion reporting are retained. The new sensitivity tables explicitly label their dispersion as standard deviation, extending the existing reporting pattern to additional results. Neither version reports random seeds, additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The principal result entries and several rankings change substantially. DPsurv's reported mean C-index, IBS, and IBLL change from 0.685, 0.288, and 0.862 in v1 Tables 1, 2, and 4 to 0.704, 0.310, and 0.824 in v2 Table 1. These are revised results under changed training/selection settings, not controlled performance gains. v2 also adds ablation, sensitivity, CONCH, runtime, expert-rating, and alternative-uncertainty results.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix D.1 adds a short proof of the previously stated survival-function bound. The GRFN derivations, mixture proof, EM updates, and GMM limiting argument are retained across relocation and notation changes. Newly numbered definitions/propositions and the numerical toy example mostly explain existing mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim dual-prototype evidential WSI survival prediction, explicit aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty, feature-to-decision interpretability, and state-of-the-art discrimination/calibration across five cancer cohorts. v2 rephrases the abstract and contributions, but retains their substantive scope; the added evaluations primarily support existing claims.

C2.justification: v1's limitations emphasize careful prototype-count selection. v2 instead interprets sensitivity results as supporting robustness and adds concrete boundaries concerning sparse tumor content, stronger domain shifts, and the pilot nature of clinical validation. It also explains the poor ablation performance of component prototypes without prevalence-weighted evidence mixing and develops λ's interpretation as controlling prediction conservativeness.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, explicitly states that GMM parameters remain fixed during evidential-network training, and provides validation/model-selection details and training-time information. Its configuration table is revised accordingly. Both versions already document initialization, baseline adaptations, optimizer settings, patch sampling, and A100 hardware.

R1.justification: Most related-work content is retained in v2 Appendix B. A new focused discussion distinguishes DPsurv's within-WSI component reasoning from Huang et al. (2024c)'s multimodal survival fusion. References are also updated through additions such as Lu et al. (2023) and several 2026 works, while some introductory citations are removed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the narrative: it condenses the introduction and main related work, adds a method overview, expands mechanism explanations, and restructures the appendices into dedicated terminology, theory, experimental, interpretation, and limitation sections. These changes extend well beyond inserting new experimental content.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. v1's separate C-index, IBS, and appendix IBLL tables are consolidated into v2 Table 1, and the configuration table is restructured. Numerous new tables and Figures 4–7 are added. Figures 1–3 retain the same graphics but are resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's lack of evidence isolating component contributions and prototype sensitivity through Table 2 and Appendix H. Additional uncertainty comparisons, extractor testing, expert ratings, and a concrete failure analysis strengthen support for the central claims and clarify applicability limits. Clearer method explanations and code-access information also help reproducibility. Changed training settings prevent interpreting the headline scores as controlled gains, and the clinical study remains preliminary, but the added controls and explicit qualifications provide a substantial overall quality improvement.
